channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: North Korea Denies Role in $6.3 Billion Binance Crypto Heist
item.description: North Korea rejected US claims that it was behind the theft of more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, after the FBI blamed Pyongyang for the biggest crypto heist on record.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Apple Sales Meet Estimates, China Is a Weak Spot
item.description: Apple posted September quarter revenue that narrowly topped analysts’ estimates, even as sales in the key Chinese market fell short of projections. Revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion during the fiscal fourth quarter, which ended Sept. 26, the company said in a statement. Analysts had estimated $113.5 billion on average, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The quarterly report — the first under new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus — offered a mixed picture to investors. Sales growth decelerated from a 16% clip in the June quarter, and results from Apple’s iPad and wearables businesses were particularly weak. But the iPhone, the company’s biggest moneymaker, remained strong. Mark Gurman, Bloomberg News Managing Editor for Global Consumer Tech, joins to discuss the results. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Looks Very Smart in Modest AI Spend: Tom Forte
item.description: Tom Forte of Maxim Group says he is especially interested in commentary on the December quarter, when the latest iPhone models will have had more time to affect sales. He said initial demand for the new iPhone duo appears strong and pointed to pent-up interest in a foldable iPhone after a long wait. He speaks with Kailey Leinz & Ed Ludlow on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: iPhone Duo Sales To Hit 7M in 2026, Predicts IDC Sr. Director
item.description: IDC Senior Director of Data & Analytics Nabila Popal says Apple’s iPhone results beating analyst expectations were not surprising. IDC’s preliminary shipment data showed iPhones outperforming a smartphone market that had suffered a historic 21% decline in calendar Q3, while Apple’s shipments fell only 4%. She speaks with Kailey Leinz & Ed Ludlow on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Grab Boosts Sales, Earnings Forecasts on Rising Ride Demand
item.description: Grab Holdings Ltd. raised its full-year revenue and profit forecasts after quarterly earnings beat estimates, signaling confidence that rising ride-hailing and food-delivery demand across Southeast Asia will offset regulatory hurdles.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Poh and Gabrielle Ng

item.title: Anthropic Taps Macquarie, CommSec for Australia IPO Retail Offer
item.description: Anthropic PBC has tapped eight firms including Macquarie Group Ltd. and Commonwealth Bank of Australia’s CommSec unit for its Australian retail offer ahead of its highly anticipated Nasdaq debut that’s set to be among the largest ever initial public offerings.
item.dc:creator: Carmeli Argana

item.title: Detroit Future City CEO: Unemployment Is Down in Detroit
item.description: Anika Goss, CEO of Detroit Future City, says the city has seen a recent population increase, driven largely by new immigrants, but is not growing as quickly or broadly as desired. Downtown investment and visible revitalization have emerged mainly over the past five to ten years, after decades of decline, and have not yet spread to communities at the pace residents would like. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Sales Slow Down, China Revenue Misses Estimates
item.description: Apple says sales slowed down in the fiscal fourth quarter, but still beat estimates. Revenue out of China missed estimates. This is the first earnings report posted under CEO John Ternus. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow and Mark Gurman report. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Isomorphic Labs President Says AI Will Design All Drugs One Day
item.description: Isomorphic Labs president Max Jaderberg thinks that artificial intelligence will be used to develop all medicines in the future — the only question is how quickly that future will arrive.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Apple’s Tightening Margins Overshadow Upbeat Holiday Forecast
item.description: Apple Inc. delivered a mixed outlook to investors in its first quarterly report under Chief Executive Officer John Ternus, with narrower profit margins overshadowing an upbeat sales forecast.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Match Falls After Quarterly Sales, Profit Outlook Miss Estimates
item.description: Match Group Inc. disappointed investors after posting weaker-than-expected quarterly revenue and forecasting adjusted earnings that missed Wall Street estimates, suggesting it still has work to do in pulling off a long-promised turnaround.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Murphy Kelly

item.title: Palantir Drops Despite Boost to Annual Revenue Outlook
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc. saw shares fall despite giving a forecast for full-year revenue that beat Wall Street’s expectations.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Martin

item.title: Nasdaq 100 Enters Correction as Megacap Results Amplify AI Fears
item.description: The Nasdaq 100 Index tumbled into a correction on Monday as investors turn increasingly pessimistic about Big Tech and the artificial intelligence trade.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: Power On: How Will a Touchscreen MacBook Impact the iPad?
item.description:
Does having a touch-screen Mac eliminate the market for the iPad?
On this episode of the Power On podcast, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman and Chris Welch discuss whether Apple's new touch-screen MacBook Pro will end up competing with its own iPad. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Binance’s $6 Billion Heist Unfolded
item.description:
In late October, hackers siphoned off more than $6 billion from crypto exchange Binance. As the company scrambles to respond, all eyes are on how the crypto industry reacts to this latest breach.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple (AAPL) Earnings: Sales Forecast Disappoints, CEO Ternus Comments
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Lumentum Goes From $1 Billion Spinoff to $115 Billion Takeover
item.description: In 2015, executives at the Silicon Valley hardware firm known then as JDSU spun off a division making optical components and commercial lasers, believing the unit would be better off chasing growth opportunities on its own.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass and Ian King

item.title: Oracle Kicks Off $20 Billion Capital Raise
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down debt offerings from Oracle, which is kicking off a $20 billion capital raise to finance its AI infrastructure spending, and Alphabet, which is tapping the European debt markets. Plus, Anthropic's revenue hits nearly $17 billion in the third quarter and Matt Witheiler, head of late-stage growth at Wellington and an Anthropic investor, joins to discuss new details from the amended IPO filing. And Apple is trading at its priciest level since 2008, ahead of its earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Will Create 'Weird' Economic Benefits: Manidis
item.description: A new essay called "The Commanding Heights" argues that as artificial intelligence becomes cheaper and more widely available, the biggest economic gains will ultimately flow to the companies best at diffusing AI into the real world. Will Manidis, co-author of the essay and SVP of Veradigm AI, discusses what he sees as the market’s mispricing of AI’s benefits and why the creators of the technology aren't always its biggest winners. Manidis joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Marvell to Acquire Lumentum in Historic $115 Billion Deal
item.description: Marvell Technology Inc. agreed to buy Lumentum Holdings Inc. at an enterprise value of $115 billion, clinching one of the largest technology deals in history in a push to capitalize on runaway data center spending.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gould, Michelle F. Davis and David Carnevali
